sections.title: Advanced Russian for Business
sections.description:
This advanced language course is designed to develop effective oral and written communication skills and competencies essential for navigating a Russian-speaking business environment. The relocation of people and companies from Belarus, Russia, and Ukraine underscores the role of the Russian language as a means of business communication in the post-Soviet countries. Consequently, the course shifts its focus from the Russian market to encompass Russian-speaking markets. Students will explore key aspects of conducting business in Russia and Kazakhstan, gaining insights into various companies and business practices through business press materials and case studies. News reports, presentations, and the final project offer opportunities to investigate other Russian-speaking markets. Special emphasis is placed on materials that focus on communication styles across diverse cultures, culture-specific behaviors, and business practices that may present challenges to effective communication among individuals from different cultural backgrounds.
In the second part of the semester, you will be working on a simulation project. The primary objective of this project is to develop a simulation that replicates a real-life business situation, allowing you to utilize and enhance your language skills, intercultural competency, and knowledge of business environment in one of the Russian-speaking countries.

sections.title: Advanced Russian for Business
sections.description: This course explores the contemporary Russian-speaking business world and develops students' ability to speak, read, and write Russian with confidence through discussion of current issues in business, economics, and geopolitics, focusing on how cultural differences shape communication and professional practices. Recent migration and business relocation from Belarus, Russia, and Ukraine have reshaped Russian-speaking professional networks across Europe, Central Asia, and beyond. Using the current business press, company profiles, case studies, and other authentic materials, the course examines business in Russia, the Baltic states, and Kazakhstan, with particular attention to regional differences in communication styles, workplace expectations, and cultural norms. The course also gives students flexibility to pursue their individual interests. Students will not only expand their vocabulary and improve fluency, but also develop the practical skills needed to follow the Russian-language press and talk about business, economics, geopolitics, and current affairs in Russian. Language pre-requisite: the course is intended for students who have completed at least one Russian-language course at the 2000 level, and for heritage speakers of Russian (students who grew up speaking Russian at home) with comparable or higher proficiency.
